definitions.explanation: An old first-person pronoun once used by men of standing; today heard only in fiction or as a joke, where it marks a speaker as grand or old-fashioned.

examples.japanese: {吾輩|わがはい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。
{吾輩|わがはい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{任|まか}せた→任せる：02417_makaseru⟧まえ。

⟦{漫画|まんが}→漫画：01511_manga⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{偉|えら}そうな⟦{博士|はかせ}→博士：03551_hakase⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧「{吾輩|わがはい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{発明|はつめい}→発明：01495_hatsumei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}よ→見る：00283_miru⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{叫|さけ}んだ→叫ぶ：02108_sakebu⟧。
examples.english: In the manga, a pompous professor shouted, "Behold my invention!"

notes:
Best known from the opening line of ⟦{夏目漱石|なつめそうせき}→夏目漱石：30575_natsumesouseki⟧'s novel {吾輩|わがはい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧ (I Am a Cat, 1905), in which a nameless cat narrates with this grand pronoun; the comedy lies in the mismatch.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{我|わ}が→我が〜：03971_waga⟧: my, our (attributive, literary)
- {拙者|せっしゃ}: I (samurai speech in period drama, humble)
- わし: I (old men in fiction and some dialects)
